Today, Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now, three hundred fifty thousand people were watching her stream, and that number was climbing fast as the broadcast moved into the Q&A segment.

If the live viewer count hit four hundred thousand, it would be an absolute world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one before her had ever pulled that off. Even the famous and obscenely rich Tony Bobbins had drawn only three hundred ninety thousand in his prime—and that was after decades in the business and with a face the whole world recognized! Now Freya had a chance to smash through that ceiling with room to spare and secure her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought it was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune smiles only on prepared minds and hands ready to act.

At first, things had gone well enough. An hour went to a lecture on how to achieve your goals. That was the most enjoyable part, but only a hundred thousand showed up. Expected, but hardly Freya’s level, with her four million on Instagram and another twelve on TikTok. Freya disliked the latter for its lack of a serious audience, but the algorithms had decided otherwise.

Another hour went to questions along the lines of “the best age to launch a startup” and “how to get up and get started,” which followers had submitted through a pre-stream form. The questions went over well and pushed the live count up to two hundred thousand.

Still, that wasn’t enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand—a plateau that grew harder and harder to push past every time.

And that was when Freya went all in, as New York wheelers and dealers liked to say. Within twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants hooked up a payment form and put up posts across social media. And so began the surprise portion of the broadcast: open questions for donations. Unmoderated, but on Freya’s terms.
